chapter: Zulu, Nice and the Punch Miller incident
title: Armstrong's last New Orleans visit and bitterness
summary: Armstrong made amends to Punch, swore never to return, and repeated this at his Long Island house.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: So anyway, Punch was happy and Louis was happy for Punch, but he swore that he'd never come back to New Orleans again for anything. Oh.
Yeah, well, I know. So, I saw him quite a few more times later on, but that was mostly in New York.

Yeah. But he didn't come back, I mean, the thing, the incident with Punch was what, 66? 66, 67 something. He didn't come, I think maybe Louis came back in 68. No, he didn't come back. I think there was a concert in 68 or not.

No, this is the concert we're talking about that was at the Loyola Fieldhouse. And that was the same concert we're talking about. That was the last one. Yeah. Must have been 68. But anyway, that was his last visit to New Orleans. Of course he only lived three more years.
Right, yeah, I was about to say.
But he was very bitter about it. Really?
Yeah. About the incident with, they talked to you about it over those next three years? Oh, yeah. About the incident with Punch? Yeah.

I was to his house in Long Island with Bobby Hackett. And we talked about it then. He said, those people there, he said, I don't know what's the matter with them. But he said, but I wouldn't go back there anymore. Those are awful people. Yeah. So that was it.
